name: committee-meeting-planner
title: Committee Meeting Planner
summary: Helps a graduate student plan, run and write up their own thesis committee meeting, from the scheduling poll to the summary of the committee's advice.
tasks: Follow up on a scheduling poll
inputs: The program's rules for committee meetings
Committee members, emails and time zones
Date and action items of the last meeting
The student's notes from the meeting
outputs: Poll email in every member's time zone
One-page summary of the committee's advice
origin_institution: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
maintainers: Talia H. Swartz, MD, PhD (Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai)
description: Helps a graduate student plan and run their own thesis committee meeting from start to finish. Use when a student says "I need to schedule my committee meeting", "help me write to my committee", "follow up on my poll", "send the calendar invite", "what should I put in my committee slides", "help me write my progress report" or "help me write up my committee meeting". Drafts every email and the calendar invite, helps prepare the slides and progress report and writes the summary afterward. Nothing is sent without the student's approval.

name: curriculum-map-builder
title: Curriculum Map Builder
summary: Builds and maintains a curriculum map that links course goals to module goals, session objectives and assessment items, and checks that every goal is taught and tested.
tasks: Check that every objective is taught and tested
Make a website of the curriculum
Update the map after schedule changes
outputs: One source spreadsheet with stable codes
origin_institution: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
maintainers: Talia H. Swartz, MD, PhD (Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai)
description: Builds and maintains a curriculum map for a whole course or program, linking course goals to module goals to session objectives to assessment items. It also checks that everything lines up. Use when an educator says "build a curriculum map", "map our course", "check that every objective is taught and tested", "which goals have no sessions", "how does our course compare with the medical school curriculum", "make a website of our curriculum" or "update the map after the schedule changed". For course directors and program leaders in graduate, MD-PhD, medical and postdoctoral programs. Produces one source spreadsheet, a gap report and a browsable map website.

name: exam-question-writer
title: Exam Question Writer
summary: Blueprints and writes objective-aligned SBA, short-answer and data-interpretation items, checked for item-writing flaws.
origin_institution: The Miriam and Aaron Gutwirth Medical School, Weizmann Institute of Science
maintainers: Amit Shraga, PhD (Weizmann Institute of Science)
description: Writes exam and practice questions aligned to learning objectives for medical and biomedical-research education — single-best-answer MCQs with clinical or research vignettes, short-answer items with rubrics, and data-interpretation items — starting from a blueprint and checking every item for known item-writing flaws. Use whenever an educator wants exam questions, quiz items, practice questions, a question bank, an assessment blueprint, or wants existing items reviewed, improved, tagged to objectives, or exported for an LMS (Moodle GIFT, CSV). Works best with the numbered objectives table from the learning-objectives-designer skill; with only a topic or material, it first drafts focused objectives. Asks whether items are for formative practice or summative assessment and adjusts rigour accordingly.

name: journal-club-planner
title: Journal Club Planner
summary: Helps a student prepare to present a research paper at journal club.
inputs: The paper, as a PDF or full text
The student's own reading of the paper and each figure
Whether they present alone or in a group, and how much time they have
The course rubric or instructions, if any
outputs: Feedback on the student's reading of each figure
A plan for splitting the paper among presenters
A slide outline with a title for each figure slide and timing
Four to six discussion questions for the student to lead
The hard questions they are most likely to get
A check against the course rubric
origin_institution: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
maintainers: Talia H. Swartz, MD, PhD (Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai)
description: Helps a student prepare to present a research paper at journal club. The student explains each figure in their own words first, and the skill checks their reading, fills gaps and explains unfamiliar methods. It then helps split the paper among presenters, plan the slides and timing, write discussion questions to lead and prepare for hard questions. Use it when a student, alone or in a group, has a journal club presentation coming up.

name: learning-objectives-designer
title: Learning Objectives Designer
summary: Extracts, writes, splits, levels and maps learning objectives; produces the numbered objectives table the other skills use.
tasks: Check alignment of objectives, activities and assessment
inputs: Course material (slides, syllabi, notebooks) or a description
origin_institution: The Miriam and Aaron Gutwirth Medical School, Weizmann Institute of Science
derived_from: New skill, building on the objectives rules in the Weizmann syllabus builder
maintainers: Amit Shraga, PhD (Weizmann Institute of Science)
description: Extracts, writes, simplifies, levels and maps learning objectives for a course, module, session or assignment in medical or biomedical-research education. Use whenever an educator wants to write or fix learning objectives, pull objectives out of existing course material (slides, syllabi, session plans, notebooks), split compound objectives into single focused ones, assign cognitive levels (Bloom or a simpler three-level scale), check alignment between objectives, activities and assessment, or map objectives to a competency framework (institutional EPAs, AAMC Foundational Competencies, GREAT MD-PhD competencies, AI competencies). Also use when asked "what are the objectives of this course", "are my objectives measurable", "map my course", or before generating exam questions or a syllabus. Produces a numbered objectives table that the syllabus-builder and exam-question-writer skills consume.

name: lesson-format-checker
title: Lesson & Notebook Format Checker
summary: Checks lesson plans and Jupyter assignment notebooks against a house-style profile and applies only approved fixes.
tasks: Create a lesson in the standard structure
origin_institution: The Miriam and Aaron Gutwirth Medical School, Weizmann Institute of Science
derived_from: Weizmann notebook format checker (generalized: profiles are pluggable; lesson plans added)
maintainers: Amit Shraga, PhD (Weizmann Institute of Science)
description: Checks a lesson plan, session plan or course/assignment Jupyter notebook against an institution's house-style format profile, reports every deviation with a proposed fix, and applies only the fixes the educator approves, in a new copy. Use whenever an educator uploads or points to a lesson plan, session plan or assignment notebook (.ipynb, .md, .docx) and asks to check, review, audit, lint, validate or "fix the format" of it, asks whether it follows the house style or template, wants timing checked against the session length, or wants a new lesson or notebook created in the standard structure. Ships with two example profiles (a Jupyter assignment-notebook profile and a generic lesson-plan profile) that institutions copy and adapt. Does not judge pedagogical quality and is not for generic data-analysis notebooks unrelated to teaching.

name: mentor-compact-creator
title: Mentor Compact Creator
summary: Builds mentoring compacts in two layers.
inputs: The trainee's stage, such as graduate student, MD-PhD student or…
The current compact, for an update
outputs: A program compact with each section marked as a program rule or as…
A side-by-side comparison of the mentor's and trainee's answers,…
Neutral questions to help the pair talk through their differences
A one-page pair agreement that sits after the program layer
A date to review the compact
origin_institution: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
maintainers: Talia H. Swartz, MD, PhD (Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai)
description: Builds mentoring compacts in two layers. A program sets up its shared compact once, with its expectations, milestones, funding, safety rules, time away and contacts. Then each mentor and trainee add their own agreements on top, like how often they meet, authorship, working hours and career goals. Use it when a program wants a compact template, when a new trainee joins a lab, when a mentor and trainee want to reset expectations or when a compact is due for its yearly review.

name: pbl-rbl-session-builder
title: PBL / RBL Session Builder
summary: Design partner for case-based PBL and tool-based RBL sessions, with readers, quizzes and intro lectures.
origin_institution: The Miriam and Aaron Gutwirth Medical School, Weizmann Institute of Science
derived_from: PBL/RBL builder used in the Weizmann MD-PhD program (course-agnostic fork)
maintainers: Amit Shraga, PhD (Weizmann Institute of Science)
description: Builds case-based PBL (problem-based learning) and tool-based RBL (research-based learning) sessions — plus their pre-session readers, comprehension quizzes, and intro lectures — for a course in ANY discipline. Use whenever someone wants to build, draft, design, revise, or improve a PBL or RBL session, a teaching case, a discovery activity, a pre-reading, a reading-comprehension quiz, or an intro lecture for active learning. The skill first asks for your course context — discipline, your students' actual stage, session format, the tools and sources you have — then applies a portable pedagogical canon — invisible pedagogy, one-inference-per-prompt step-width, predict-before-reveal, the productive trap, information-release discipline, figures-as-tasks, and a warm-collegial facilitator voice with no AI effusiveness. It calibrates every prompt to the student stage you specify, never invents sources or citations, and works as a design partner that catches AI failure modes before they reach a draft.

name: reading-material-generator
title: Reading Material Generator
summary: Turns papers and chapters into session-sized interactive readings with glossary, reflection prompts and self-checks.
tasks: Turn a paper into reading material
origin_institution: The Miriam and Aaron Gutwirth Medical School, Weizmann Institute of Science
derived_from: Reading generator used in the Weizmann MD-PhD program
maintainers: Amit Shraga, PhD (Weizmann Institute of Science)
description: Turns one or more source documents (journal papers, book chapters, reviews, protocols) into structured, interactive reading material sized for a real class session in medical or biomedical-research education. Use whenever an educator asks for reading material, a pre-reading, a group reading assignment, a flipped-classroom reading, or wants to turn a paper or chapter into something learners read before or during a lecture, PBL, RBL or workshop — even without the phrase "reading material". Triggers include "turn this paper into something my students can read", "I need the reading part of my session", "make a group reading out of this chapter", "summarize this paper for a 2-hour session". Also use to shorten or lengthen an existing reading, add a glossary, add discussion questions, or add figures from the source.

name: syllabus-builder
title: Syllabus Builder
summary: Builds or updates a syllabus from partial course material, with an evidence-based (E/P/X) map to any competency framework.
tasks: Map a course to competencies or EPAs
origin_institution: The Miriam and Aaron Gutwirth Medical School, Weizmann Institute of Science
derived_from: Weizmann syllabus builder (generalized: framework and template are now pluggable)
maintainers: Amit Shraga, PhD (Weizmann Institute of Science)
description: Builds or updates a course syllabus from whatever course material exists (complete or partial) and maps the course to the institution's competency framework with evidence-based rules — institutional EPAs, AAMC Foundational Competencies, the AAMC GREAT MD-PhD competencies, AI competencies, or any framework the educator supplies. For course leaders in medical, MD-PhD, PhD and biomedical-research programs, any course kind (block, module, longitudinal track, lab course, elective) and any teaching format (lecture, PBL, RBL, TBL, CBL, simulation, labs, journal club). Use whenever someone wants to create, draft, fill in, update or review a syllabus or course outline; map a course or assignment to competencies, EPAs or milestones; check which competencies a course covers or where its gaps are; or says "here are my course materials, make the syllabus" — even with only an outline, a few slide decks or a verbal description.
